newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ report on Peters allegations due within weeks.
newsitem.headline: NZ report on Peters allegations due within weeks.

text.p: A New Zealand parliamentary committee report investigating an assault complaint against Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters is likely to be released in the next fortnight, officials said on Thursday.
Privileges committee chairman and Attorney-General Paul East told reporters that, after an hour-long meeting of the committee on Wednesday evening, it still had issues to resolve.
East said a report would not be made to parliament during Thursday, but "certainly within the next week or two".
He said it was possible the issues could be resolved without another formal meeting of the committee.
East declined to say if more talks would be held with Peters.

"We're considering some suggestions that various members have put forward with regard to our final report. We're giving those matters some thought and we hope to be able to resolve the matter in the very near future," he said.
The contempt allegation against Peters was made by left-wing Alliance leader Jim Anderton after a fracas between Peters and government backbencher John Banks on March 5.
Banks and Anderton said in evidence that Peters had assaulted and threatened Banks outside the debating chamber after a late-night parliamentary debate on legislation to delay tax cuts.
Peters said he only put a hand on Banks to indicate he wanted to continue talking.
The committee's report had been expected when parliament resumed on Tuesday this week.
When it is finally delivered it is likely to be the focus of an extensive debate, with each of parliament's 120 members theoretically entitled to speak for 10 minutes.
The privileges committee also heard a complaint, lodged by Anderton as a petition to the committee, about a separate incident on March 5.

Anderton alleged Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare manhandled a radio journalist who was trying to record the exchange between Banks and Peters. Henare has apologised to the journalist for the incident.
